title: Dress for the site
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Select clean, fitted workwear that suits site rules, weather, mobility and contamination risk.
Explain why loose sleeves, jewellery and hair must be secured around moving equipment.
Separate uniform requirements from task-specific protective equipment and replace clothing that is torn, contaminated or unsafe.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Overview
instruction.body: This lesson develops practical competence in dress for the site for routine professional cleaning work. Apply the employer’s site procedures and stop if a task falls outside your training or authority.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Select clean, fitted workwear appropriate to site rules, weather, mobility and contamination risk. Loose items can catch in machinery.

instruction.heading: Prepare and verify
instruction.body: Check the site dress requirements, weather, task and exposure risks before selecting clothing. Wear clean, fitted garments that permit bending and movement; secure loose sleeves, jewellery and hair around moving equipment.

instruction.heading: Perform the work safely and professionally
instruction.body: Separate normal uniform requirements from protective equipment requirements. A branded shirt is not protection against splashes; select task-specific PPE based on the risk assessment, product label and site procedure.

instruction.heading: Check, record and escalate
instruction.body: Replace clothing that is torn, contaminated or unsafe. Keep a spare clean layer where a shift involves changing environments or customer-facing work.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Check the site dress requirements, weather, task and exposure risks before choosing clothing.
Wear clean, fitted workwear that allows bending and movement.
Secure loose sleeves, jewellery and hair before working near moving equipment, because loose items can catch in machinery.
Keep normal uniform separate from protective equipment, and do not treat a branded shirt as splash protection.
Select task-specific protective equipment from the risk assessment, the product label and the site procedure.
Replace clothing that is torn, contaminated or unsafe, and note the defect.
Keep a spare clean layer where a shift involves changing environments or customer-facing work.
Stop and ask the supervisor before going further if a task falls outside your training or authority.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Site dress rules, weather, task and exposure risks are checked before clothing is chosen.
Loose sleeves, jewellery and hair are secured around moving equipment.
Protective gear is matched to each job's hazard review, label and site procedure rather than to a generic tick-list.
Torn, contaminated or unsafe clothing is replaced, and a spare clean layer is kept where the shift changes environments.
summary: The cleaner selects clean, fitted workwear that suits the site rules, the weather, mobility and the contamination risk.
Loose sleeves, jewellery and hair are secured around moving equipment, because loose items can catch in machinery.
Uniform requirements are kept separate from task-specific protective equipment, and torn, contaminated or unsafe clothing is replaced.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do if the uniform you have does not suit an unfamiliar task?
options: Continue if you are wearing the right clothing
Use a branded shirt as protection, since it is what you have
Stop, and ask the supervisor before going further
Change into a loose top so you can move more easily

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a torn or contaminated uniform item be handed over?
options: Wear it anyway until the end of the shift
Note the defect, replace the unsafe item and tell the supervisor
Hide the torn item under a jacket so the client does not see
Wait for the next uniform order without telling anyone

knowledgeChecks.question: How should protective equipment be chosen, separately from the uniform?
options: Wear the branded shirt as splash protection and skip the gloves for the day
Choose the PPE nearest to hand, since it is the usual item and the one most often worn
Pick task-specific PPE from the risk assessment, product label and site procedure
Use the same gloves for every product, since they are in the kit today

knowledgeChecks.question: Identify the unsafe alternative
options: Wearing PPE selected from the risk assessment
Relying on a branded shirt as splash protection
Securing loose sleeves and hair around moving equipment
Replacing clothing that is torn or contaminated

knowledgeChecks.question: Describe the record or escalation needed
options: Clothing defects can be noted in the next shift's briefing and worn again until then
A note of the defect and replacement, with the supervisor told if the item was unsafe
A verbal mention to a colleague only and the defect is kept on the rack for the day
Photographs of the clothing posted in a personal chat with the client's name on the photo
